1. **High — `src/Mod/Part/Gui/Command.cpp:1974`**  
   The first selected curve is assigned to `curve2` instead of `curve1`. Selecting two edges and invoking **Part Ruled Surface** leaves `curve1` null; with two edges from one object, `curve2` is overwritten by the second edge. The command then fails validation or attempts creation without the first curve.

2. **High — `src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.cpp:1334`**  
   `simplificationPriority` contains `TopAbs_SHELL` twice and omits `TopAbs_EDGE`. If a requested shape resolves to a compound containing exactly one open edge, `simplifyCompound()` returns the compound rather than the edge. Callers such as extrusion/revolution axis extraction then receive a compound where an edge is required and reject the axis or raise a shape-type error.

3. **Medium — `src/Mod/PartDesign/App/FeatureSketchBased.cpp:730`**  
   This branch now calls `getShape()` rather than `getTopoShape()`. `getShape()` forcibly adds `NoElementMap`, and converting its raw `TopoDS_Shape` back to `TopoShape` cannot restore the source tag, hasher, or element map. For an up-to-shape selection containing a mapped wire that is converted into a face, the generated face loses its source-element provenance; after upstream topology changes, downstream element naming can become unstable or associate with the wrong generated face.

**1. src/Mod/Part/Gui/Command.cpp:1973 — `curve1` silently renamed to `curve2`**
The old code `curve1 = Part::Feature::getTopoShape(docobj1, subnames1[0]...)` became `curve2 = ...` in the same branch that sets `link1 = subnames1[0]`. The `link1` line was left unchanged, proving `curve1` was intended. Failure scenario: user selects one edge on object 1 and one edge on object 2 and runs CmdPartRuledSurface (the normal two-edge route). `curve1` is never assigned (stays a null `TopoDS_Shape`) while `curve2` gets object 1's edge and is then overwritten by object 2's edge in the `subnames2` block. The ruled surface is then built from a null first curve — invalid/garbage feature or exception — for every single-edge-per-object selection. Same when two edges are picked on object 1 only (`subnames1.size()==2`): `curve1` stays null.

**2. src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.cpp:1333 — `simplifyCompound` drops `TopAbs_EDGE` and duplicates `TopAbs_SHELL`**
The old inline simplification chain was SOLID, COMPSOLID, FACE, SHELL, **EDGE**, WIRE, VERTEX. The new 7-element array has SHELL twice (lines 1332–1333) and no EDGE. Failure scenario: any `NeedSubElement` caller whose reference resolves to a compound containing exactly one edge (e.g. an edge inside a Part compound, a single-edge wire delivered as a compound) now receives the whole compound where the old code returned the single `TopoDS_Edge`. Concrete breakage: `DlgExtrusion.cpp`'s gate checks `sub.ShapeType() == TopAbs_EDGE` — the compound fails the check and the user cannot select that axis; `Extrusion::fetchAxisLink`/`Revolution::fetchAxisLink` feed the result into `TopoDS::Edge(axEdge)`/`BRepAdaptor_Curve`, which throw or produce garbage on a compound. The duplicate SHELL entry also makes the 7-length array only cover 6 types.

**3. src/Mod/Part/Gui/Mirroring.cpp:104 — shape fetched for `sSubName` while the gate still checks `subString`**
Old code passed `subString.c_str()`; the new call passes `sSubName`, but the surrounding logic (emptiness check at line 102 and the `strstr(subString.c_str(), "Face")` classification at line 105) still uses `subString`. Failure scenario: if `sSubName` is a different variable (e.g. the raw selection subname or an uninitialized member), the fetched shape no longer corresponds to the face being tested — `getTopoShape` may return the whole object's shape or a null shape, so the mirror-plane gate approves/rejects on the wrong geometry, or `shape` is null and the mirror is built from nothing. If `sSubName` doesn't exist in this class, the file fails to compile. The class body is not in the diff, so I can't pin which of the two, but the variable identity change versus the old line is in the diff.

**4. src/Mod/PartDesign/App/FeatureSketchBased.cpp:729-734 — element map discarded before `makeElementFace` in `getUpToShapeFromLinkSubList`**
Old: `getTopoShape(ref, subString.c_str(), true)` returns a `TopoShape` that still carries its element map/hasher/tag, which is copied into `face` and used by `makeElementFace()`. New: `getShape(...)` forces `NoElementMap` (new `getShape` does `options | NoElementMap`) and returns a bare `TopoDS_Shape`; the reconstructed `TopoShape face = shape;` therefore has no element map, no hasher, and tag 0 when `makeElementFace()` runs. Failure scenario: a pad/pocket "Up to face"/"Up to last" built from a linked sub-face creates the terminating face with no mapped element name; after an upstream geometry change renames elements, the feature has no traceable element to map back to, breaking the toponaming/reference chain (constraint or face reference resolves to the wrong element or fails on recompute). The tag loss also severs the source association that `makeElementFace` relied on.

**5. src/Mod/Part/Gui/TaskSweep.cpp:302 — loop indexes `subnames[0]` instead of `*it`**
The loop iterates `it` over `subnames` but pushes `getTopoShape(docobj, subnames[0]...)` each time (retained verbatim from the old line, but this hunk is the rewrite — the bug is visible in the diff). Failure scenario: in the Sweep task, when the user selects more than one profile edge and the profile is stored with multiple subnames, every pushed subshape is the first selected edge; the sweep is generated from the same first edge N times instead of from each selected edge, producing a wrong profile/sweep (or failing the multi-edge profile requirement).

Also noted: `FeatureBlendCurve.cpp:139` switches `getTopoShape(...).getShape()` to `getShape(...)`, but since the caller discards the `TopoShape` wrapper immediately, the forced `NoElementMap` is not observable there — no defect reported. The `FeatureHole` `DontSimplifyCompound` (FeatureHole.cpp:1831) and `AppPartPy.cpp` flag-expression changes appear semantically equivalent to the old calls; I found no failure scenario for them.## Defect Analysis

### 1. `src/Mod/Import/App/ExportOCAF2.cpp:384-388`

**Defect: Incorrect bitwise operation for `Transform` flag**
```cpp
Part::Feature::Transform * (!sub)
```
`Transform` is an enum value (4), not a boolean. Multiplying it by `!sub` (0 or 1) yields either 0 or 4, which *happens* to work for this single flag but is semantically wrong and breaks if combined with other flags. The correct pattern used elsewhere is `(Feature::Transform * Base::asBoolean(transform))` or `options | Feature::Transform`.

**Failure scenario:** If `sub` is empty string (`!sub == true`), `Transform * 1 = 4` (correct). If `sub` is non-empty (`!sub == false`), `Transform * 0 = 0` (correct for this flag alone). But this pattern is fragile and inconsistent with the rest of the codebase.

---

### 2. `src/Mod/Measure/App/Measurement.cpp:128-135` and `761-768` (two hunks)

**Defect: Missing `DontSimplifyCompound` flag where it may be needed**
The new code passes `NeedSubElement | ResolveLink | Transform` but omits `DontSimplifyCompound`. The old code had `needSubElement=true` and `transform=true` with `resolveLink=true` (default). The simplification logic in `getTopoShape` (lines 1300-1318 in PartFeature.cpp) now triggers when `NeedSubElement` is set AND `DontSimplifyCompound` is NOT set. This changes behavior: previously a compound shape with a single solid would be simplified; now it will be simplified *only if* `NeedSubElement` is set. For measurement operations, this could return a different sub-shape than expected.

**Failure scenario:** A linked object returns a compound containing exactly one solid. Old code: returned the compound (since `needSubElement=true` but the simplification logic didn't exist or worked differently). New code: returns the solid directly, losing the compound structure. Downstream code expecting a compound gets a solid.

---

### 3. `src/Mod/Part/App/AppPartPy.cpp:2291-2298`

**Defect: Operator precedence bug in flag composition**
```cpp
(Feature::ResolveLink * resolveLink) | 
(Feature::NeedSubElement * Base::asBoolean(needSubElement) | 
(Feature::Transform * Base::asBoolean(transform)) | 
(Feature::NoElementMap * Base::asBoolean(noElementMap)))
```
Missing closing parenthesis for the second line. The `|` between `NeedSubElement * ...` and `Transform * ...` groups as:
```cpp
(Feature::NeedSubElement * Base::asBoolean(needSubElement) | (Feature::Transform * Base::asBoolean(transform))
```
Then this result is ORed with `NoElementMap * ...`. But the `ResolveLink * resolveLink` is ORed with the entire rest. This *might* parse correctly due to precedence (`*` before `|`), but the missing `)` on line 2293 makes it a syntax error or wrong grouping.

**Failure scenario:** Compilation error, or if it compiles (due to implicit grouping), wrong flags passed. For example if `needSubElement=true, transform=false, noElementMap=true`: `NeedSubElement | 0 | NoElementMap` = correct. But the parentheses mismatch is a definite bug.

---

### 4. `src/Mod/Part/App/Attacher.cpp:884-890`

**Defect: Missing `DontSimplifyCompound` flag**
Same issue as Measurement.cpp. The attacher extracts sub-shapes for attachment logic. If the source shape is a compound with a single face, it will now be simplified to that face, potentially breaking attachment logic that expects the compound structure.

**Failure scenario:** Attaching to a compound face in a multi-body PartDesign feature. The compound gets simplified to a single face, losing the compound context needed for correct attachment mapping.

---

### 5. `src/Mod/Part/App/FeatureExtrusion.cpp:173-177` (first hunk)

**Defect: Missing `DontSimplifyCompound` flag**
Same pattern. Axis edge extraction from a compound could return a simplified edge instead of the compound.

**Failure scenario:** Extrusion axis linked to a compound edge (e.g., from a fused shape). Simplification returns a single edge, changing the axis direction/location.

### 6. `src/Mod/Part/App/FeatureExtrusion.cpp:267` (second hunk)

**Defect: Signature mismatch - `getShape` call missing `options` parameter**
```cpp
TopoDS_Shape sh = Feature::getShape(shapeLink.getValue(), nullptr, &mat, &docobj);
```
The new signature is `getShape(obj, subname, pmat, powner, options)`. This call passes 4 arguments but the new signature expects 5 (with `options` having a default). However, the default in the header is `ResolveLink | Transform`. The old call had `resolveLink=false, transform=false` (since `getShape` old signature: `needSubElement=false, pmat, powner, resolveLink=false, transform=true` — wait, let me check).

Old `getShape` signature (from diff context): `getShape(obj, subname, needSubElement, pmat, powner, resolveLink, transform)`
Call: `getShape(shapeLink.getValue(), nullptr, false, &mat, &docobj)` → `needSubElement=false, pmat=&mat, powner=&docobj, resolveLink=default(true), transform=default(true)`

New signature: `getShape(obj, subname, pmat, powner, options=ResolveLink|Transform)`
Call: `getShape(shapeLink.getValue(), nullptr, &mat, &docobj)` → `subname=nullptr, pmat=&mat, powner=&docobj, options=default(ResolveLink|Transform)`

**Behavior change:** Old: `resolveLink=true, transform=true`. New: `options=ResolveLink|Transform` (same). But old also had `needSubElement=false` which is now implicit (not in options). This seems OK *if* the default options match. However, the old call explicitly passed `false` for `needSubElement` (3rd param), which in the new signature maps to `pmat`. Wait — the parameter order changed!

Old: `(obj, subname, needSubElement, pmat, powner, resolveLink, transform)`
New: `(obj, subname, pmat, powner, options)`

The call `getShape(shapeLink.getValue(), nullptr, &mat, &docobj)` in old code:
- `obj` = shapeLink.getValue()
- `subname` = nullptr
- `needSubElement` = false (but this is passed as 3rd arg)
- `pmat` = &mat (4th arg)
- `powner` = &docobj (5th arg)

In new code, the 3rd arg is `pmat`, 4th is `powner`. So `&mat` goes to `pmat`, `&docobj` goes to `powner` — **this matches by accident** because both are pointer types. But `needSubElement=false` is dropped. The new default options include `ResolveLink|Transform`, which matches the old defaults. So this *happens* to work but is fragile.

**Failure scenario:** If someone changes the default options in the header, this call silently gets different behavior. Also, if `needSubElement` was ever `true` here, it would be lost.

---

### 10. `src/Mod/Part/App/MeasureClient.cpp:100-101` (first hunk)

**Defect: Signature mismatch - wrong argument count/order**
```cpp

```
Old: `getTopoShape(obj, subname, needSubElement, pmat, powner, resolveLink, transform, noElementMap)` — 8 params.

- `subname` = subject.getElementName()
- `pmat` = mat (Base::Matrix4D*)
- `powner` = nullptr
- `options` = **missing!** Uses default `ResolveLink | Transform`

**But:** Old call had `needSubElement=false` (3rd arg). New call passes `mat` as 3rd arg (which is `pmat`). The `needSubElement=false` is dropped. The old `resolveLink=true` (6th arg) maps to default options `ResolveLink|Transform`. So `Transform` is *added* compared to old (old had `transform` defaulting to `true`? Let me check old signature defaults).

From PartFeature.h old: `getTopoShape(..., bool needSubElement=false, Base::Matrix4D* pmat=nullptr, App::DocumentObject** powner=nullptr, bool resolveLink=true, bool transform=true, bool noElementMap=false)`

Old call: `getTopoShape(obj, subname, false, mat, nullptr, true)` → `needSubElement=false, pmat=mat, powner=nullptr, resolveLink=true, transform=default(true), noElementMap=default(false)`

New call: `getTopoShape(obj, subname, mat, nullptr)` → `pmat=mat, powner=nullptr, options=default(ResolveLink|Transform)`

**Behavior change:** Old: `transform=true` (applied). New: `Transform` in options (applied). Same. But `needSubElement=false` is now implicit (not in options). This is OK *if* the subname is not a sub-element reference. But `subject.getElementName()` returns a sub-element name! So `NeedSubElement` should be set.

**Failure scenario:** `subject.getElementName()` returns "Face1". Old code: `needSubElement=false` → sub-element name stripped, whole shape returned. New code: `NeedSubElement` not set → same behavior (sub-element stripped). But the *intent* of `getLocatedShape` is to get the *located* sub-shape. The function name suggests it should respect the sub-element. This is a pre-existing bug potentially, but the new code doesn't fix it — it preserves the bug.

Wait, looking at the old call more carefully: `getTopoShape(obj, subject.getElementName(), false, mat, nullptr, true)` — the 3rd arg is `needSubElement=false`. So it explicitly did NOT want sub-element resolution. The new call drops this, so it uses default options which include `ResolveLink|Transform` but NOT `NeedSubElement`. So behavior is preserved. But is this correct for `getLocatedShape`? The function applies the matrix to locate the shape. If the sub-element name is stripped, it gets the whole shape's location, not the sub-element's. This seems wrong but is pre-existing.

## Summary of Defects Found

### Critical Defects (Runtime failures / Wrong behavior)

1. **`src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.cpp:1307`** (in `simplifyCompound`): **Duplicate `TopAbs_SHELL` entry and missing `TopAbs_EDGE` in simplification priority array.** A compound with a single edge will not be simplified (returns compound instead of edge), breaking all callers using `NeedSubElement` without `DontSimplifyCompound`.

2. **`src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.cpp:673`** (in `getElementFromSource`): **`Transform` flag dropped** — call passes `ResolveLink` only, losing default `Transform`. Sub-shapes returned in local coordinates instead of global, breaking element mapping for transformed objects.
3. **`src/Mod/Part/Gui/Mirroring.cpp:103`**: **Undefined variable `sSubName`** used instead of `subString` — compilation error or wrong sub-name.
4. **`src/Mod/Part/Gui/TaskSweep.cpp:304`**: **Loop variable unused** — always passes `subnames[0]` instead of `*it`. Pre-existing bug, not fixed.
5. **`src/Mod/Part/App/AppPartPy.cpp:2293`**: **Missing closing parenthesis** in flag expression — syntax error or wrong operator grouping.

6. **`src/Mod/PartDesign/App/FeatureSketchBased.h:135`**: **Default `getProfileShape()` options missing `DontSimplifyCompound`** — all ProfileBased features (Extrude, Revolve, Loft, etc.) get unwanted compound simplification by default.

7. **`src/Mod/Part/App/PartFeature.cpp:1186`** (internal `_getTopoShape` call in `getElementFromSource`): **Inconsistent flags** — passes only `NeedSubElement`, no `ResolveLink`/`Transform`. Differs from new defaults, may break link traversal in element mapping.

---
